label: Person
name: Alan Hopes
summary:
Alan Hopes (b. 1944) is a British Catholic bishop who serves as Bishop of East Anglia, notable as a former Anglican priest who converted to Catholicism and was subsequently ordained a Catholic priest and later consecrated bishop. Born in Oxford, he was ordained an Anglican deacon in 1969 and served as a Church of England clergyman for over two decades before his reception into the Catholic Church in 1994.

Hopes received under the pastoral provision established by Pope John Paul II that allowed married former Anglican clergy to be ordained as Catholic priests. His priestly ordination as a Catholic in 1995 and his eventual appointment as auxiliary bishop of Westminster (2003) and later Bishop of East Anglia (2013) made his journey one of the most prominent examples of Anglican-to-Catholic ministerial transition in modern British Church history.

His personal journey embodied both the Anglican-Catholic theological convergence of the Agreed Statements and the continuing institutional divisions that prompted some Anglicans to seek full communion with Rome. As Bishop of East Anglia, he leads a diocese that includes some of England's historically important recusant Catholic communities. His distinctive biography—Anglican priest to Catholic bishop—has made him a significant figure in ecumenical conversations about ministerial orders and Church unity.
